summary: Limon Municipal Airport (LIC/KLIC) is a small general aviation airport serving the town of Limon, Colorado, located on the high plains roughly 90 miles southeast of Denver along Interstate 70. The facility primarily supports private pilots, recreational flying, and occasional business or emergency aviation activity for the surrounding Lincoln County region. Its open prairie setting and clear skies make it a popular refueling stop for cross-country flights across the central United States.
faqs:
Q: Does Limon Municipal Airport offer commercial airline service?
A: No, the airport is not served by commercial airlines and operates exclusively as a general aviation facility for private and recreational flights.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features a single runway, aircraft parking areas, and basic services suitable for small private aircraft. Pilots should check current conditions with the airport manager before arrival.

Q: Can I fly into Limon as a transient or visiting pilot?
A: Yes, the airport accommodates transient pilots, though it is recommended to confirm fuel availability and any landing fees in advance.

Q: What is the closest major airport to Limon?
A: Denver International Airport (DEN) is approximately 90 miles to the northwest and offers the nearest full-service commercial aviation options.
transport_tips: Reaching the airport typically requires a personal vehicle, as Limon is a rural community without public transit links to the airfield. The airport sits just northwest of town and is a short drive from Interstate 70, making it accessible for travelers arriving by car. Rental cars are available in Limon itself, though options are limited, so arranging ground transport in advance is advisable.
local_tip: When flying into Limon, plan your fuel stops carefully—the town is small and airport services may be limited outside business hours, so contacting the local fixed-base operator ahead of time ensures a smooth arrival.
